themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked 363% this week to 180 complaints vs. 38.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.87), signaling a sudden infrastructure deterioration across CD 107 requiring urgent investigation into root cause and scope.
evidence: 180 street condition complaints this week vs. 38.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Represents most statistically significant spike in 311 data this reporting period
reporting_angles: Site inspection of specific streets generating complaints to identify patterns (potholes, flooding, subsidence, salt damage from winter)
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and whether this week's spike reflects deferred repair backlog or acute event (weather, utility work, construction)

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints surged 900% last week to 5 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.36), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, suggesting a new or intensifying activity disrupting park use.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Baseline was near-zero, making spike particularly stark and actionable
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Central, Riverside, others) generated complaints and what specific activities are causing noise (events, construction, amplified sound)
Speak with parks enforcement and community members about whether a new vendor, event permit, or ongoing activity initiated recently

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped 586% last week to 12 complaints vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.73), indicating emerging tensions over post-pandemic outdoor seating—likely sidewalk obstruction, noise, or sanitation issues.
evidence: 12 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Suggests rapid shift in resident sentiment toward outdoor seating or enforcement change
reporting_angles: Map outdoor dining complaints geographically to identify hotspot blocks and restaurant corridors (Columbus Ave, Amsterdam Ave, etc.)

Interview residents and restaurant owners about specific grievances (table placement blocking sidewalks, noise late at night, poor waste management) and whether this reflects new establishments or seasonal expansion

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Alert
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints increased 700% two weeks ago to 4 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95), a low-volume but statistically severe spike warranting urgent clarification of substance types and locations.
evidence: 4 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Historically rare complaint type, making spike noteworthy for environmental/health risk
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 complaint logs to identify specific substances and addresses (chemical spills, asbestos, fuel, etc.)
Cross-check with Asbestos spike (357% increase, 4 complaints 2 weeks ago) to determine if renovation/demolition activity is source

themes_detail.label: Asbestos & Renovation Risk
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked 357% two weeks ago to 4 complaints vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.0), correlating with elevated DOB alteration filings (1032 filed in 90 days) and suggesting under-managed building renovation hazards.
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% increase, z-score: 4.0)
1032 alteration permits filed in prior 90 days—highest permit activity type in district
Convergence of asbestos spike + hazardous materials spike + high alteration volume suggests renovation-related exposure risk
reporting_angles: Analyze DOB permit data to identify clusters of alteration work and cross-reference with asbestos complaint addresses
Investigate whether DOB is adequately enforcing asbestos survey and notification requirements during renovations; interview affected residents and tenants about exposure
